claim: Individual cortical neurons must integrate broadly over space yet simultaneously obtain sharp tuning to specific global stimulus features.
source: Individual neurons must integrate broadly over space, yet simultaneously obtain sharp tuning to specific global stimulus features.
evidence: This is a statement of the research problem being addressed in the manuscript.

claim: The logic for how single neurons summate over their spatial inputs has been well explored in anesthetized animals.
source: Although the logic for how single neurons summate over their spatial inputs has been well explored in anesthetized animals, how large groups of neurons compose a flexible population code of higher-order features in awake animals is not known.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of prior research in the field.

claim: How large groups of neurons compose a flexible population code of higher-order features in awake animals is not known.
source: Although the logic for how single neurons summate over their spatial inputs has been well explored in anesthetized animals, how large groups of neurons compose a flexible population code of higher-order features in awake animals is not known.
evidence: This is a statement identifying a gap in current knowledge.

claim: A novel tactile stimulator was developed that allowed precise measurement of spatial summation in actively whisking mice.
source: We developed a novel tactile stimulator that allowed the precise measurement of spatial summation even in actively whisking mice.
evidence: This describes a methodological development reported in the manuscript.

claim: A sparse but comprehensive population code for higher-order tactile features was found in somatosensory cortex.
source: Using this system, we found a sparse but comprehensive population code for higher-order tactile features that depends on a heterogeneous and neuron-specific logic of spatial summation beyond the receptive field.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The population code for higher-order tactile features depends on a heterogeneous and neuron-specific logic of spatial summation beyond the receptive field.
source: Using this system, we found a sparse but comprehensive population code for higher-order tactile features that depends on a heterogeneous and neuron-specific logic of spatial summation beyond the receptive field.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the mechanism underlying the population code.

claim: Different somatosensory cortical neurons summed specific combinations of sensory inputs supra-linearly.
source: Different somatosensory cortical neurons summed specific combinations of sensory inputs supra-linearly, but integrated other inputs sub-linearly, leading to selective responses to higher-order features.
evidence: This is a primary finding about how individual neurons integrate inputs.

claim: Different somatosensory cortical neurons integrated other inputs sub-linearly.
source: Different somatosensory cortical neurons summed specific combinations of sensory inputs supra-linearly, but integrated other inputs sub-linearly, leading to selective responses to higher-order features.
evidence: This is a primary finding about how individual neurons integrate inputs.

claim: Supra-linear and sub-linear summation leads to selective responses to higher-order features.
source: Different somatosensory cortical neurons summed specific combinations of sensory inputs supra-linearly, but integrated other inputs sub-linearly, leading to selective responses to higher-order features.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional consequence of the observed summation patterns.

claim: Visual cortical populations employed a nearly identical scheme to generate a comprehensive population code for contextual stimuli.
source: Visual cortical populations employed a nearly identical scheme to generate a comprehensive population code for contextual stimuli.
evidence: This is a primary finding showing the generality of the mechanism across cortical areas.

claim: Heterogeneous logic of input-specific supra-linear summation may represent a widespread cortical mechanism for the synthesis of sparse higher-order feature codes in neural populations.
source: These results suggest that a heterogeneous logic of input-specific supra-linear summation may represent a widespread cortical mechanism for the synthesis of sparse higher-order feature codes in neural populations.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings in two cortical areas.

claim: The heterogeneous summation mechanism may explain how the brain exploits the thalamocortical expansion of dimensionality to encode arbitrary complex features of sensory stimuli.
source: This may explain how the brain exploits the thalamocortical expansion of dimensionality to encode arbitrary complex features of sensory stimuli.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the broader significance of the findings.

claim: Stimulus features beyond the receptive field potently modulate a neuron's coding properties.
source: Although neurons are primarily driven by specific patterns of sensory drive within their receptive field, stimulus features beyond the receptive field potently modulate a neuron's coding properties.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Stimuli outside a neuron's receptive field can facilitate its firing rate when combined with stimulation in its receptive field.
source: In some instances, stimuli that on their own drive no activity in a neuron can facilitate its firing rate when combined with stimulation in its receptive field (Ego-Stengel et al., 2005; Estebanez et al., 2016; Hirata and Castro-Alamancos, 2008; Ramirez et al., 2014; Shimegi et al., 1999), but far more frequently they drive suppression (Adesnik et al., 2012; Angelucci et al., 2017; Arabzadeh et al., 2003; Bair et al., 2003; Blakemore and Tobin, 1972; Brumberg et al., 1996; Cavanaugh et al., 2002; Dipoppa et al., 2018; Ego-Stengel et al., 2005; Fanselow and Nicolelis, 1999; Gilbert, 1977; Kato et al., 2017; Mirabella et al., 2001; Ozeki et al., 2009; Shushruth et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Stimuli outside a neuron's receptive field far more frequently drive suppression than facilitation.
source: In some instances, stimuli that on their own drive no activity in a neuron can facilitate its firing rate when combined with stimulation in its receptive field (Ego-Stengel et al., 2005; Estebanez et al., 2016; Hirata and Castro-Alamancos, 2008; Ramirez et al., 2014; Shimegi et al., 1999), but far more frequently they drive suppression (Adesnik et al., 2012; Angelucci et al., 2017; Arabzadeh et al., 2003; Bair et al., 2003; Blakemore and Tobin, 1972; Brumberg et al., 1996; Cavanaugh et al., 2002; Dipoppa et al., 2018; Ego-Stengel et al., 2005; Fanselow and Nicolelis, 1999; Gilbert, 1977; Kato et al., 2017; Mirabella et al., 2001; Ozeki et al., 2009; Shushruth et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In the barrel cortex, even the best contextual stimulus for a neuron typically approximates linear summation of its component inputs.
source: In the barrel cortex, even the best contextual stimulus for a neuron typically approximates linear summation of its component inputs (Laboy-Juárez et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Suppression can improve information coding and efficiency.
source: Although suppression can improve information coding and efficiency (Crochet et al., 2011; Froudarakis et al., 2014; Sachdev et al., 2012; Vinje and Gallant, 2000), sharpen feature selectivity (Angelucci et al., 2017; Jacob et al., 2008) and enhance saliency and boundary detection (Li, 1999; Li, 2009), supra-linear summation to highly specific combinations of inputs could represent a powerful means by which cortical neurons might compute and selectively encode higher-order features of sensory stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Suppression can sharpen feature selectivity.
source: Although suppression can improve information coding and efficiency (Crochet et al., 2011; Froudarakis et al., 2014; Sachdev et al., 2012; Vinje and Gallant, 2000), sharpen feature selectivity (Angelucci et al., 2017; Jacob et al., 2008) and enhance saliency and boundary detection (Li, 1999; Li, 2009), supra-linear summation to highly specific combinations of inputs could represent a powerful means by which cortical neurons might compute and selectively encode higher-order features of sensory stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Suppression can enhance saliency and boundary detection.
source: Although suppression can improve information coding and efficiency (Crochet et al., 2011; Froudarakis et al., 2014; Sachdev et al., 2012; Vinje and Gallant, 2000), sharpen feature selectivity (Angelucci et al., 2017; Jacob et al., 2008) and enhance saliency and boundary detection (Li, 1999; Li, 2009), supra-linear summation to highly specific combinations of inputs could represent a powerful means by which cortical neurons might compute and selectively encode higher-order features of sensory stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Supra-linear summation to highly specific combinations of inputs could represent a powerful means by which cortical neurons might compute and selectively encode higher-order features of sensory stimuli.
source: Although suppression can improve information coding and efficiency (Crochet et al., 2011; Froudarakis et al., 2014; Sachdev et al., 2012; Vinje and Gallant, 2000), sharpen feature selectivity (Angelucci et al., 2017; Jacob et al., 2008) and enhance saliency and boundary detection (Li, 1999; Li, 2009), supra-linear summation to highly specific combinations of inputs could represent a powerful means by which cortical neurons might compute and selectively encode higher-order features of sensory stimuli.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: In the primary visual cortex, specific contextual stimuli have been shown to facilitate responses in a supra-linear manner.
source: In the primary visual cortex, specific contextual stimuli have been shown to facilitate responses in a supra-linear manner, although the underlying logic is not well understood (Levitt and Lund, 1997; Sillito et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The underlying logic of supra-linear facilitation in primary visual cortex is not well understood.
source: In the primary visual cortex, specific contextual stimuli have been shown to facilitate responses in a supra-linear manner, although the underlying logic is not well understood (Levitt and Lund, 1997; Sillito et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: How the brain builds a comprehensive population code that covers the high-dimensional space of global stimulus properties remains unknown.
source: Despite extensive prior investigation of the logic of contextual summation on the individual neuron level (Angelucci et al., 2017; Armstrong-James and Callahan, 1991; Bair et al., 2003; Blakemore and Tobin, 1972; Boloori and Stanley, 2006; Brecht et al., 2003; Brecht and Sakmann, 2002; Brumberg et al., 1996; Gilbert, 1977; Higley and Contreras, 2003; Moore and Nelson, 1998; Simons, 1985; Simons and Carvell, 1989), how the brain builds a comprehensive population code that covers the high-dimensional space of global stimulus properties remains unknown.
evidence: This is a statement identifying a gap in current knowledge despite extensive prior research.

claim: If all neurons summated their surround inputs in a similar fashion, contextual modulation would primarily act to scale activity but not generate new coding properties.
source: If all neurons summated their surround inputs in a similar fashion, contextual modulation would primarily act to scale activity but not generate new coding properties.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what would happen under a specific condition.

claim: If different neurons in a population integrated their contextual inputs uniquely, selectivity for more complex sensory stimuli could emerge across neural ensembles.
source: If instead different neurons in a population integrated their contextual inputs uniquely, selectivity for more complex sensory stimuli could emerge across neural ensembles.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what could happen under a different condition.

claim: Primary sensory cortical neurons massively outnumber their thalamic inputs, permitting overcomplete representations.
source: Primary sensory cortical neurons massively outnumber their thalamic inputs, permitting overcomplete representations.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Theoretical and experimental work has proposed that overcompleteness permits sparse representations, in which small groups of active neurons efficiently represent natural or complex inputs.
source: Theoretical and experimental work has proposed that overcompleteness permits sparse representations, in which small groups of active neurons efficiently represent natural or complex inputs (Barlow, 1961; de Vries et al., 2020; Lewicki and Sejnowski, 2000; Olshausen and Field, 1997; Stringer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior theoretical and experimental work.

claim: The diversity and specificity of supra-linear summation yields a sparse, comprehensive population code for complex spatial features.
source: We found that the diversity and specificity of this supra-linear summation yields a sparse, comprehensive population code for complex spatial features.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Each possible combination of whiskers or visual stimulus patches drives activity in a dedicated, similarly sized population of neurons.
source: In particular, each possible combination of whiskers or visual stimulus patches drives activity in a dedicated, similarly sized population of neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The heterogeneous summation mechanism may be critical for the ability of cortical populations to encode arbitrary complex stimuli.
source: This mechanism may thus be critical for the ability of cortical populations to encode arbitrary complex stimuli.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the findings.

claim: Awake mice were head-fixed on a rotary treadmill and habituated to run at relatively high speed (>30 cm/s).
source: Awake mice were head-fixed on a rotary treadmill and habituated to run at relatively high speed ( >30 cm/s), a condition in which they moved their whiskers in a rhythmic and stereotyped fashion for many minutes at a time with a protracted set point (Pluta et al., 2015; Pluta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: At high running speeds, mice moved their whiskers in a rhythmic and stereotyped fashion for many minutes at a time with a protracted set point.
source: Awake mice were head-fixed on a rotary treadmill and habituated to run at relatively high speed ( >30 cm/s), a condition in which they moved their whiskers in a rhythmic and stereotyped fashion for many minutes at a time with a protracted set point (Pluta et al., 2015; Pluta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research and describes observed behavior.

claim: All but five of the largest whiskers were completely trimmed just before the experiment.
source: All but five of the largest whiskers were completely trimmed just before the experiment, and data was collected in the next 1–2 hr prior to the onset of any trimming-induced plasticity (Clem and Barth, 2006; Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Data was collected in the next 1-2 hours prior to the onset of any trimming-induced plasticity.
source: All but five of the largest whiskers were completely trimmed just before the experiment, and data was collected in the next 1–2 hr prior to the onset of any trimming-induced plasticity (Clem and Barth, 2006; Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods, with citations supporting the timing to avoid plasticity.

claim: On each trial, the whiskers made repeated active touches (13.1±5.9 touches, mean ± s.d.) with the presented set of pistons.
source: Using this system, we found a sparse but comprehensive population code for higher-order tactile features that depends on a heterogeneous and neuron-specific logic of spatial summation beyond the receptive field. Different somatosensory cortical neurons summed specific combinations of sensory inputs supra-linearly, but integrated other inputs sub-linearly, leading to selective responses to higher-order features.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: Slight trimming of the five whiskers ensured that one and only one whisker made contact with each piston.
source: Importantly, slight trimming of these five whiskers ensured that one and only one whisker made contact with each piston, which we confirmed using high-speed imaging (Figure 1C; ).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods, confirmed by high-speed imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 48% (2262/4756) of identified neurons showed a significant response to at least one of the 31 stimuli.
source: Forty-eight percent (2262/4756) of identified neurons showed a significant response (see Materials and methods) to at least one of the 31 stimuli.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: 52% of responsive neurons exhibited a significant response to just one of the single whisker stimuli.
source: When the pistons were presented individually to map the 'receptive field' of each touch-responsive neuron, 52% of responsive neurons exhibited a significant response to just one of the single whisker stimuli, and 12.6% responded to two or more.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: 12.6% of responsive neurons responded to two or more single whisker stimuli.
source: When the pistons were presented individually to map the 'receptive field' of each touch-responsive neuron, 52% of responsive neurons exhibited a significant response to just one of the single whisker stimuli, and 12.6% responded to two or more.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: 34.8% of responsive neurons did not respond to any single whisker stimulus, but responded robustly to at least one multi-whisker combination.
source: However, a striking 34.8% did not respond to any single whisker stimulus, but responded robustly to at least one multi-whisker combination.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: Both L4 and L2/3 excitatory neurons organized into loose spatial maps of preferred whiskers consistent with prior findings from anesthetized mice.
source: Both L4 and L2/3 excitatory neurons organized into loose spatial maps of preferred whiskers consistent with prior findings from anesthetized mice (Clancy et al., 2015; Kerr et al., 2007; Sato et al., 2007; Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data, supported by citations to prior research and shown in figures.

claim: Most neurons summed specific combinations of inputs highly supra-linearly during active whisking in awake mice.
source: Unlike most of the prior studies, we found that most neurons summed specific combinations of inputs highly supra-linearly.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: All 31 stimuli were represented approximately evenly across all imaged mice.
source: Importantly, across all imaged mice, all 31 stimuli were represented approximately evenly (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Barrel cortex has the ability to sparsely encode all possible higher-order tactile stimuli in the five-whisker space probed.
source: This demonstrates that barrel cortex has the ability to sparsely encode all possible higher-order tactile stimuli in the five-whisker space we probed.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The population code for multi-whisker stimuli correlated well with selective supra-linear summation for the most preferred stimulus.
source: Comparing the stimulus selectivity and deviation from linear summation from each neuron side by side shows that the population code for multi-whisker stimuli correlated well with selective supra-linear summation for the most preferred stimulus (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3B and D.

claim: For most whisker combinations, summation was sub-linear (i.e. suppressive).
source: This supports the idea that stimulus-specific summation over surround whiskers helps promote a sparse and selective code for higher-order tactile features: for most whisker combinations, summation was sub-linear (i.e. suppressive, consistent with prior findings).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: For a small subset of multi-whisker inputs summation was strongly supra-linear.
source: However, for a small subset of multi-whisker inputs summation was strongly supra-linear.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: The best stimulus for each neuron nearly always contained the principal whisker.
source: Another important rule emerged from this analysis: the best stimulus for each neuron nearly always contained the principal whisker (PW), demonstrating that it was required for the preferred supra-linear response (71% of neurons in C1 column, see Materials and methods, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C.

claim: 71% of neurons in C1 column had the principal whisker in their best stimulus.
source: Another important rule emerged from this analysis: the best stimulus for each neuron nearly always contained the principal whisker (PW), demonstrating that it was required for the preferred supra-linear response (71% of neurons in C1 column, see Materials and methods, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: The preferred stimulus almost always included the anatomically aligned 'columnar' whisker even when the CW and PW were different.
source: The preferred stimulus also almost always included the anatomically aligned 'columnar' whisker (CW) even when the CW and PW were different (60% of C1 neurons' PW was C1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 60% of C1 neurons' principal whisker was C1.
source: The preferred stimulus also almost always included the anatomically aligned 'columnar' whisker (CW) even when the CW and PW were different (60% of C1 neurons' PW was C1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: Sparse neural ensembles in both L4 and L2/3 encoded the complete set of the 31 presented second-order tactile stimuli.
source: We next compared the population codes in L4 (2,428 neurons) and L2/3 (2,328 neurons): first, we found that sparse neural ensembles in both layers encoded the complete set of the 31 presented second-order tactile stimuli (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), implying that even at the first stage of cortical processing cortical integration gives rise to a sparse, comprehensive code for higher-order stimuli.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Even at the first stage of cortical processing (L4) cortical integration gives rise to a sparse, comprehensive code for higher-order stimuli.
source: We next compared the population codes in L4 (2,428 neurons) and L2/3 (2,328 neurons): first, we found that sparse neural ensembles in both layers encoded the complete set of the 31 presented second-order tactile stimuli (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), implying that even at the first stage of cortical processing cortical integration gives rise to a sparse, comprehensive code for higher-order stimuli.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: In L4, the principal whisker contributed substantially more to the individual neurons' responses than in L2/3.
source: However, we observed several important differences indicative of a translaminar transformation of the neural codes for these features. In L4, the PW contributed substantially more to the individual neurons' responses than in L2/3.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing experimental data between layers.

claim: In L2/3, the surround whiskers, often in highly specific and non-contiguous combinations, shaped the tuning to multi-whisker stimuli.
source: Conversely, in L2/3, the surround whiskers, often in highly specific and non-contiguous combinations, shaped the tuning to multi-whisker stimuli.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: A much greater fraction of L2/3 neurons responded more specifically to unique combinations of whiskers than in L4.
source: Ultimately, as a consequence, a much greater fraction of L2/3 neurons responded more specifically to unique combinations of whiskers, than in L4.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing experimental data between layers.

claim: More than three times as many L2/3 neurons as in L4 exhibited multi-whisker receptive fields.
source: More than three times as many L2/3 neurons as in L4 exhibited multi-whisker receptive fields (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), and L2/3 neurons were substantially less selective for single whisker stimuli (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: L2/3 neurons were substantially less selective for single whisker stimuli than L4 neurons.
source: More than three times as many L2/3 neurons as in L4 exhibited multi-whisker receptive fields (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), and L2/3 neurons were substantially less selective for single whisker stimuli (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, E.

claim: L2/3 had nearly three times the number of neurons that exhibited driven responses for a multi-whisker stimulus that did not include the principal whisker (14 vs. 43%).
source: Strikingly, L2/3 had nearly three times the number of neurons that exhibited driven responses for a multi-whisker stimulus that did not include the PW (14 vs. 43%; Extended data. Figure 3—figure supplement 2F, G) implying a more diverse code for complex tactile features.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F, G.

claim: L2/3 had a greater fraction of neurons whose preferred stimulus lacked the 'columnar whisker' compared to L4.
source: L2/3 also had a greater fraction of neurons whose preferred stimulus lacked the 'columnar whisker' (analysis restricted to the C1 column, Figure 3—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Among C1 column neurons, the contribution of the C1 whisker to neuronal tuning curves was significantly more distributed in L2/3 than for L4 neurons.
source: Similarly, among these C1 column neurons, the contribution of the C1 whisker to neuronal tuning curves was significantly more distributed than for L4 neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2I.

claim: L2/3 could faithfully represent the combination of whiskers in a given stimulus with a more spatially compact population of neurons.
source: These differences suggest that L2/3 could faithfully represent the combination of whiskers in a given stimulus with a more spatially compact population of neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: V1 populations encoded all possible combinations of the five stimulus patches in approximately even fashion.
source: As in the barrel cortex, responses to single patch stimuli reflected the underlying topographic map (Figure 4B). In agreement with the notion of diverse, stimulus-specific summation, we likewise observed that V1 populations encoded all possible combinations of the five stimulus patches in approximately even fashion (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 4C and E.

claim: Many V1 neurons summed grating patches supra-linearly to give rise to their preferred stimulus, but summed nearly all other stimuli sub-linearly.
source: Moreover, just as in the barrel cortex, many V1 neurons summed these grating patches supra-linearly to give rise to their preferred stimulus, but summed nearly all other stimuli sub-linearly, effectively sharpening the tuning to the preferred stimulus (Figure 4D and F).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 4D and F.

claim: The coding principle of stimulus-specific summation was shared across layer 4 and layer 2/3 in V1.
source: As in barrel cortex (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), this coding principle was shared across layer 4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B) and layer 2/3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sub-linear summation dominated for all but the most preferred stimuli in multi-whisker or multi-patch preferring neurons across both cortical areas.
source: We found that in multi-whisker or multi-patch preferring neurons across both cortical areas, sub-linear summation dominated for all but the most preferred stimuli (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Supra-linear summation was highly selective for only the most preferred stimulus on average across both cortical areas and layers.
source: In contrast, supra-linear summation was highly selective for only the most preferred stimulus on average across both cortical areas and layers.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: The most preferred stimulus evoked significantly more supra-linear responses than the average non-preferred stimulus in a substantial fraction of neurons in both S1 and V1.
source: Across all layers and areas, the most preferred stimulus evoked significantly more supra-linear responses than the average non-preferred stimulus in a substantial fraction of neurons in both S1 and V1 (Figure 5E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Within the measurement error of tuning curve estimates, a simple linear-nonlinear model (GLM) was able to capture the stimulus-specific supra- and sub-linear summation observed.
source: Thus, we concluded that within the measurement error of our tuning curve estimates, a simple linear-nonlinear model was able to capture the stimulus-specific supra- and sub-linear summation we observed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on model fitting to the experimental data.

claim: The GLM significantly outperformed the oracle model on average across layers and cortical areas.
source: Indeed, we found that across layers and cortical areas, the GLM significantly outperformed the oracle model on average (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, column 4; p<10–4, Wilcoxon signed-rank test).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis of model performance shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transformation from action potential rate to GCaMP6s fluorescence changes was approximately linear and highly sensitive to firing rate changes (mean Pearson's correlation coefficient=0.71±0.03).
source: We found this transformation to be approximately linear and highly sensitive to firing rate changes (mean Pearson's correlation coefficient=0.71±0.03, mean ± s.e.m., n=21), consistent with prior findings (Chen et al., 2013; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from calibration experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2, supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Stimulus-specific behavioral adaptation in the mouse's whisking could not have contributed to the stimulus-specific supra-linear facilitation observed.
source: These data imply that stimulus-specific behavioral adaptation in the mouse's whisking could not have contributed to the stimulus-specific supra-linear facilitation we observed, although it may have led to a general trend of modestly weaker sensory responses for stimuli containing an increasing number of pistons that would be systematic across all neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the whisker tracking data.

claim: Population responses in anesthetized mice were not as uniformly distributed across multi-whisker space as in awake, whisking mice, and instead favored broader spatial summation.
source: Population responses in these anesthetized mice were not as uniformly distributed across multi-whisker space as in awake, whisking mice, and instead favored broader spatial summation, or in other words, exhibited poorer feature selectivity (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A, C, E).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing experimental data between awake and anesthetized conditions shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A, C, E.

claim: L2/3 tuning curves in awake mice were substantially less well fit by a general linear model than in anesthetized mice, potentially owing to enhanced nonlinearity in the awake, active condition.
source: Furthermore, L2/3 tuning curves in awake mice were substantially less well fit by a general linear model, potentially owing to enhanced nonlinearity in the awake, active condition (Figure 3—figure supplement 4F).
evidence: This is a finding from model fitting analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4F, with a speculative interpretation.

claim: Anesthesia and passive touch linearize summation in L2/3 of the barrel cortex and alter the population code of higher-order features.
source: These results imply that anesthesia and passive touch linearize summation in L2/3 of the barrel cortex and alter the population code of higher-order features.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings comparing awake and anesthetized conditions.

claim: A precise but heterogeneous logic of spatial summation in the sensory cortex leads to the generation of a sparse comprehensive feature code for complex tactile or visual stimuli.
source: Our data show that a precise but heterogeneous logic of spatial summation in the sensory cortex leads to the generation of a sparse comprehensive feature code for complex tactile or visual stimuli.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The activity of barrel or visual cortical neurons, particularly in the awake, active state, could be potently facilitated by highly specific subsets of surround stimuli.
source: We found that the activity of barrel or visual cortical neurons, particularly in the awake, active state, could be potently facilitated by highly specific subsets of surround stimuli, and many neurons could only be driven by more complex spatial features.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Many neurons could only be driven by more complex spatial features.
source: We found that the activity of barrel or visual cortical neurons, particularly in the awake, active state, could be potently facilitated by highly specific subsets of surround stimuli, and many neurons could only be driven by more complex spatial features.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: In each neuron, surround facilitation was highly specific to just one or a small number of multi-whisker combinations.
source: In each neuron, this surround facilitation was highly specific to just one or a small number of multi-whisker combinations, while most other combinations suppressed or had no impact on the response to preferred stimuli.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Most other combinations suppressed or had no impact on the response to preferred stimuli.
source: In each neuron, this surround facilitation was highly specific to just one or a small number of multi-whisker combinations, while most other combinations suppressed or had no impact on the response to preferred stimuli.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Across simultaneously imaged populations within a small region of the sensory cortex, the logic of surround summation was sufficiently diverse that ensembles of co-activated neurons could sparsely and uniquely encode any of the presented higher-order stimuli.
source: Most importantly, across simultaneously imaged populations within a small region of the sensory cortex, the logic of surround summation was sufficiently diverse that ensembles of co-activated neurons could sparsely and uniquely encode any of the presented higher-order stimuli.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: A small, but relatively uniform fraction of the imaged neurons encoded each of the presented stimuli.
